---
title: "masbayes: Bayesian Genomic Prediction for SNP and Multi-allelic Markers"
---

## masbayes: Bayesian Genomic Prediction for SNP and Multi-allelic Markers {.unnumbered}


### Description

Implements BayesR (four-class mixture prior) and BayesA
(marker-specific variance prior) for genomic prediction using biallelic
SNP or multi-allelic markers. Both methods are available as full MCMC
or stochastic EM; continuous (Gaussian) and binary (probit) traits are
supported natively via a high-performance Rust backend.



### Statistical model

The general linear model shared by BayesR and BayesA is:

<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">y = \mathbf{1}\mu + W\beta + \varepsilon,
  \quad \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,\sigma_e^2 I)</code>


where $y$ is the phenotype vector, $\mu$ is the intercept,
$W$ is the marker design matrix (from
<code>construct_wah_matrix</code> for multi-allelic or
<code>construct_snp_matrix</code> for SNP markers), $\beta$ is
the vector of allele effects, and $\sigma_e^2$ is the residual
variance. When fixed effects are included:

<p style="text-align: center;">$y = \mathbf{1}\mu + X\alpha + W\beta + \varepsilon$




### General assumptions


<ul>
<li> Phenotypic observations are conditionally independent given the
genetic and fixed effects.

</li>
<li> Residuals $\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,\sigma_e^2 I)$;
for binary traits the probit model with Albert-Chib data augmentation
is used (liability scale, $\sigma_e^2 = 1$).

</li>
<li> Allele effects $\beta_j$ are a priori independent across
loci; the prior distribution differs between BayesR and BayesA.

</li>
<li> The design matrix $W$ is centred (column mean zero) to
ensure identifiability of the intercept $\mu$.

</li>
<li> For multi-allelic markers the most-frequent allele per block is
treated as the baseline reference and excluded from $W$.

</li></ul>



### How the model works (marker level)

masbayes estimates allele effects <em>individually</em> at the marker
level, rather than aggregating them into a population-level relationship
matrix.

<strong>BayesR</strong> places a four-component mixture prior on each allele
effect (Erbe et al., 2012):

<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">\beta_j \mid \pi,\,\sigma_\beta^2 \;\sim\;
  \pi_0\,\mathcal{N}(0,0)
  + \pi_1\,\mathcal{N}(0,\,0.001\sigma_\beta^2)
  + \pi_2\,\mathcal{N}(0,\,0.01\sigma_\beta^2)
  + \pi_3\,\mathcal{N}(0,\,0.1\sigma_\beta^2)</code>


Most alleles are shrunk to zero ($\pi_0$), while a small proportion
carry small, medium, or large effects — enabling implicit variable
selection.

<strong>BayesA</strong> assigns each allele a marker-specific variance from a
scaled inverse chi-squared distribution (Meuwissen et al., 2001):

<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">\beta_j \mid \sigma_{\beta_j}^2 \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,\sigma_{\beta_j}^2),
  \quad \sigma_{\beta_j}^2 \sim \chi^{-2}(\nu,\,S^2)</code>


allowing heavier-tailed effect-size distributions than ridge regression.

Posterior parameters are inferred via MCMC (Gibbs sampling) or
stochastic EM. Genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs) are computed
by summing posterior mean allele effects across all loci:

<p style="text-align: center;">$\widehat{g}_i = \hat{\mu} + \mathbf{w}_i^\top \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$


Heritability is estimated as
<code class="reqn">h^2 = \mathrm{Var}(W\hat{\beta}) /
  [\mathrm{Var}(W\hat{\beta}) + \hat{\sigma}_e^2]</code>.



### Main functions


<dl>
<dt><code>construct_wah_matrix</code></dt><dd>Build the multi-allelic
$W_{\alpha h}$ design matrix from phased haplotype data.
</dd>
<dt><code>construct_snp_matrix</code></dt><dd>Build the SNP design matrix
(VanRaden centering or z-score standardisation).
</dd>
<dt><code>run_bayesr</code></dt><dd>Fit BayesR (four-class mixture).
</dd>
<dt><code>run_bayesa</code></dt><dd>Fit BayesA (marker-specific variance).
</dd>
<dt><code>predict.masbayes_bayesr</code>,
<code>predict.masbayes_bayesa</code></dt><dd>Predict GEBVs and compute
accuracy metrics (S3 methods).
</dd>
<dt><code>summary.masbayes_bayesr</code>,
<code>summary.masbayes_bayesa</code></dt><dd>Full posterior report
including $h^2$, ESS, Geweke, and variance components (S3
methods).
</dd>
</dl>
